pm.status_title.en: Validation status: reviewed calculation, not certified

pm.status.en: These Panchanga values are calculated from the recorded birth details using the stated astronomical methods and Swiss Ephemeris. Independent engineering tests checked the calculation rules, event boundaries, and selected published lunar-phase references. These results are not certified for religious observances or muhurta. Please confirm important timings with a trusted local Panchang.

v.status.en: These times are calculated, not observed or certified. Another Panchang may use a different sunrise rule or reference city, so its times can differ, sometimes by many minutes. For religious observances, follow your trusted local Panchang or family priest.

v.intro.en: The Vara is the weekday of the Panchanga. It runs from one local sunrise to the next, so a birth before sunrise keeps the Vara of the previous day. Sunrise and sunset are calculated for the birthplace shown on page {birth}.

v.m.checks_value.en: The calculation was cross-checked against an independent astronomical model and compared with published sunrise tables. These are calculated times under stated assumptions, not observations; published times may differ by location, method and minute rounding.

v.m.convention_value.en: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) rule, applied at the birthplace: the Sun's upper edge on the horizon, with 31′ refraction and 16′ semidiameter (its centre 47′ below the horizon); sunset uses the same rule. IMD's national Panchang day starts at a Central Station's sunrise; IMD also prints four-city tables.

v.m.times_value.en: Rounded to the nearest minute, shown as "about"; actual sunrise can differ with weather and the horizon.

v.near.en: The birth is within {minutes} minutes of the calculated sunrise (rounded times can show the same minute). A small error in the recorded time, another sunrise convention or the real horizon at the birthplace could put the birth on the other side of sunrise and change the Vara. The {minutes}-minute band is a cautious review prompt, not a measured accuracy.
